text.p: French industrial group Alcatel Alsthom SA rose to a 12-month high on Tuesday, boosted by heartening 1996 results.
Traders reported a mixed market for most American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) as they followed the sagging larger New York markets.
The Dow industrials dipped in mid-morning trade amid concern about the prospect of higher interest rates.

Alcatel rose 1-7/8 to 23-1/2, a 12-month high, after the conglomerate reported a small profit for last year following a record loss in 1995. The company's chairman also told analysts Alcatel should have satisfactory profits in 1998.
Volume was a moderate 134,000 shares and was dominated by two block trades totaling 112,500 shares. Further details about the trades were not immediately available.
Most Latin American ADRs were flat. Mexican bellwether Telefonos de Mexico rose 1/4 to 40, and one Latin American trader said, "That seems to be the standout this morning."
British Steel Plc rose 1/4 to 25-3/8 as a bid by Germany's Krupp for Thyssen AG vorm August Thyssen-Huette raised hopes of a shakeout in the European steel industry.
Australia's News Corp fell 1/2 to 20 in reaction to its takeover of U.S. marketing and broadcasting company Heritage Media.
Decliners led advancers 254 to 170 among 806 ADRs. The index was off 0.24 percent in late morning and volume was 20 million shares.
